---
title: "Next steps toward a current pollock MSE"
date: 2026-10-09
lightbox: true
---

## 1. Freeze a coherent input package

Select the intended assessment implementation and annual run explicitly. Obtain
the accepted model-ready input package or designate an exploratory update. Resolve
the `pm_25.dat` weight-row inconsistencies, identify current catches and their
revision date, and select current BTS, ATS, AVO, fishery CAA, and weight products.
Confirm geographic coverage, units, sample sizes, missing observations, and age
error. The 2026 workbook is a collection of products with different vintages.

**Completion evidence:** an immutable input manifest with source, version/date,
hash, units, year and age dimensions, missing-data rules, and adoption status.
All dimensions reconcile; no zero-fill or unrecorded row truncation occurs.

## 2. Choose and validate the assessment-to-OM bridge

Prefer direct export from a coherent validated pollock assessment for the reference
OM. Maintain the SAMtool SCA as a documented simplified alternative if it serves
a specific question. Export N-at-age, F-at-age, natural mortality, maturity,
weights, recruitment conventions, spawning timing, and terminal selectivity.
Resolve separate spawning/fishery weights and the age-0/age-1/15+ boundary.

`Assess2OM` expects jointly sampled assessment arrays and leaves observation and
implementation settings to the user; see its
[official documentation](https://msetool.openmse.com/reference/Assess2OM.html).
Test the historical reconstruction before simulating future management.

**Completion evidence:** catch, survival transitions including the plus group,
biomass, SSB, and recruitment agree with the exported run to declared tolerances.
Report gradients < 1e-4, Hessian checks, uncertainty, and bounds for every fitted
run used. Avoid comparing objective values across incompatible likelihoods or
observation sets.

## 3. Define the OM ensemble and observation process

Use validated posterior or bootstrap draws; retain parameter correlations.
Resolve the published posterior mixing/ESS checks before selecting Model 26.0
draws. Introduce structural cases for recruitment, mortality, weights, and
selectivity based on the scientific question. Specify historical and future
survey schedules, errors, composition sample sizes, assessment lags, and
implementation error. Preserve missing 2020 BTS observations and the documented
ATS 2020 data omissions where relevant to the selected reference input.

**Completion evidence:** each simulation has a traceable draw/scenario identity,
the observed and simulated data processes match intended assumptions, and an
annual assessment/advice step closes the feedback loop.

## 4. Implement the management procedures and objectives

Write the current pollock Tier 3 reference procedure from the accepted specification
with explicit F40%/F35% reference points, biomass adjustments, catch constraints,
and assessment/advice timing. Confirm which operational features belong in this
study, including fleet allocation, ecosystem-wide constraints, bycatch limits,
and implementation shortfalls. Treat benchmark reference MPs as performance bounds.

Agree on short-term and long-term yield, biomass-limit event probability,
rebuilding time, annual catch variability, and any bycatch/ecosystem objectives.
State time windows and whether an indicator is conditional on a scenario,
averaged over simulations, or measured within a simulation.

**Completion evidence:** hand-calculated test cases reproduce each MP's catch
advice, all stock-status plots use the intended biomass and F reference points,
and a corrected Slick export matches the underlying MSE arrays.

## 5. Run a pilot, then check simulation precision

Start with a small reproducible pilot for dimensions, missingness, numerical
stability, and advice timing. Increase simulations only after it passes. For each
key risk and yield indicator, examine Monte Carlo uncertainty and MP rank
stability; choose the simulation count using that evidence. The existing 48
replicated histories are a development setting, not evidence of decision precision.

**Completion evidence:** saved OM/MSE objects, a run manifest, reviewed numerical
failures, correctly aligned reference-point arrays, seed and package versions,
and intervals on reported performance measures.

## 6. Produce the analytical report and review record

Move computation into a script or dependency-aware workflow. Let Quarto consume
saved validated tables and figures. Add residuals, convergence, retrospectives,
hindcast checks, uncertainty, sensitivity comparisons, and clear conclusions.
Record proposed, reviewed, and adopted changes separately. Review alt text,
keyboard access, table headers, and screen-reader behavior before a formal release.

The repository can grow a wiki with **Home**, **Data dictionary**, **Survey products
and vintages**, **Assessment-to-OM mapping**, **Management procedures**, **Validation
gates**, and **Annual change log**. The Pages site supplies the initial public
documentation; a separate wiki has not been populated in this release.
